causal-factors.name: CDU polling lead in February 2026 polls
causal-factors.rationale: Polls consistently show CDU leading Greens by roughly 27–29% to 22–25%, supporting CDU as the largest party.

causal-factors.name: Greens closing gap in some polls
causal-factors.rationale: Several polls show Greens narrowing the gap (e.g., CDU 27–29% vs Greens 25–27% in ZDF/ARD and CDU 28% vs Greens 22–23% in others), reducing CDU's margin.

causal-factors.name: FGW seat projection (CDU 35 vs Greens 32)
causal-factors.rationale: FGW's projection places CDU ahead in seats, reinforcing CDU as the largest party.

causal-factors.name: Historical base-rate favoring Greens (2016, 2021)
causal-factors.rationale: Historical results show Greens led seat counts in 2016 and 2021, tempering CDU's probability of finishing with the most seats.

causal-factors.name: Prediction markets and consensus placing CDU first
causal-factors.rationale: Prediction markets and expert polls broadly anticipate CDU as the leading party, supporting the CDU-first outcome.

causal-factors.name: Electoral-system dynamics (MMP) and coalition realities
causal-factors.rationale: The mixed-member system can yield seat outcomes that diverge from vote shares, introducing some uncertainty but not decisively reversing the lead.

causal-factors.name: CDU polling lead and FGW seat projection
causal-factors.rationale: Multiple February 2026 polls show CDU ahead of Greens (~27–29% vs ~22–25%), and FGW projects CDU as the largest party (CDU 35 seats vs Greens 32), boosting the probability CDU wins the most seats.

causal-factors.name: Prediction markets and consensus CDU finishes first
causal-factors.rationale: Polychance and other polls indicate CDU first, with markets leaning toward CDU winning the most seats, reinforcing the uptrend.

causal-factors.name: Historical Greens leadership in 2016 and 2021
causal-factors.rationale: Historical precedent shows Greens have led seat counts in prior elections, suggesting CDU cannot be assumed to win the most seats solely from current polls.

causal-factors.name: Greens closing the gap and increased uncertainty in late February polls
causal-factors.rationale: Greens narrowing the gap (CDU ~27–29% vs Greens ~23–25%) increases uncertainty about the seat outcome and reduces CDU's edge.

causal-factors.name: AfD's persistent vote share limiting CDU's seat advantage
causal-factors.rationale: AfD polling around 19–21% siphons votes away from CDU and can translate into seat losses, reducing CDU's likelihood of finishing first in seats.

causal-factors.name: Mixed-member proportional electoral dynamics (seat distribution vs vote share)
causal-factors.rationale: The Baden-Württemberg system can amplify or dampen vote-to-seat translation, introducing uncertainty about whether CDU will edge out Greens in seat count even with a vote lead.

causal-factors.name: CDU lead in late-February polls with FGW seat projection
causal-factors.rationale: Late-February polls place CDU around 27–29% and Greens around 21–25%, and FGW projects CDU 35 seats to Greens 32, supporting CDU as the largest party. ([politpro.eu](https://politpro.eu/de/baden-wuerttemberg/wahlumfragen/forschungsgruppe-wahlen-2026-02-26/landtagswahl?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Greens closing the gap in late-February polls
causal-factors.rationale: INSA (Feb 23–26) shows CDU 28% and Greens 22%, with other polls indicating Greens gaining ground, which could erode CDU's lead. ([politpro.eu](https://politpro.eu/en/baden-wuerttemberg/opinion-polls/insa-2026-02-23/state-election?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Historical precedent and base-rate uncertainty
causal-factors.rationale: Historically, CDU led in 2011 while the Greens were the largest party in 2016, illustrating that the current CDU lead is not a guaranteed predictor of winning the most seats. ([en.wikipedia.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2011_Baden-W%C3%BCrttemberg_state_election?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: Green leadership and Cem Özdemir as Spitzenkandidat
causal-factors.rationale: The Greens' nomination of Cem Özdemir as Spitzenkandidat could energize their campaign and sustain momentum ahead of election day. ([welt.de](https://www.welt.de/article693c850e87262f1e6c470fa9?utm_source=openai))

causal-factors.name: End-stage campaign momentum and parity pressure
causal-factors.rationale: Late-stage coverage shows CDU ahead but Greens closing toward parity, creating a more competitive race with uncertain implications for seat outcomes. ([zdf.de](https://www.zdf.de/magazine/zdfheute-live-102/landtagswahl-bw-wahlkampf-video-100?utm_source=openai))
